# Final Reader Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos renews each chamber before the next control receives its name;
Awtsmoos.com should let each rewrite reduce accidental complexity while deepening the reader's flame.

## Phase 1 — source reality

1. Read both reader-control CSS files fully.
2. Read main reader style import topology and line counts.
3. Read typography, sidebar, popover, panel-initialization, and listener entry modules.
4. Trace exact consumers and existing reader tests.
5. Record concrete defects only from source evidence.

## Phase 2 — coherent code tranche

6. If shell CSS contains mixed responsibilities or exceeds the vessel boundary, split it into an import-only manifest plus focused local modules.
7. Introduce reader-local layer/safe-area tokens only if the current source lacks a coherent equivalent.
8. Rewrite typography/sidebar/popover gates only where actual lifecycle/state debt exists.
9. Preserve existing IDs and public module exports.
10. Keep daily controls primary; fold advanced groups through existing semantic disclosure instead of new permanent chrome.
11. Do not modify the HTML template unless source tracing proves markup changes are necessary.

## Phase 3 — verification and expansion

12. Re-read every touched file from disk.
13. Audit tabs, line counts, selector ownership, numeric z-index, viewport hazards, and compressed meaningful logic.
14. Run existing preference, utility, command-palette, node-DOM, and reader-control tests.
15. Run browser/mobile geometry if a reader harness exists; otherwise use the existing local server/Chrome path.
16. Compare planned versus actual and write the delta.
17. Continue to Heichelos directory quality, profile/aliases, comments, notifications, composer, and editors after reader verification closes.

## Expected first write set

No production file is committed to the write set until Phase 1 inspection is complete. The design target is the smallest coherent set that fixes proven reader-shell debt without duplicating existing architecture.
